evals.prompt:
Audit this checkout form component before we ship:
Payment
Invalid
Pay
Target is WCAG 2.2 AA.
assertions: Opens with a coverage note stating what markup alone can and cannot verify (e.g. actual screen-reader output, live focus order)
Every finding cites a specific success criterion with number, name, and level (e.g. 2.1.1 Keyboard [A], 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value [A])
Every finding names the user group and assistive tech it blocks (e.g. keyboard-only, NVDA/VoiceOver users)
The div-as-button is a blocker for keyboard and screen-reader users; minor issues like the lock icon's alt text are not inflated to blocker
Contrast for #999 on #fff is given as a computed ratio (about 2.85:1) against the 4.5:1 threshold, and the 20x20 target is checked against 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum
Each finding is tagged [auto] or [manual] and has a concrete fix
Ends with a 'what's solid' section and a must-verify-with-live-AT checklist
Does not claim a pass on any behavior the markup can't show, and does not invent elements not in the snippet

evals.prompt: I'm on the digital team at Harrowgate District Libraries. Our event booking page is booking.html with styles.css, and our automated scanner's output is scan-report.txt - it says we pass. Before we put a 'WCAG 2.2 AA compliant' badge on the site, please confirm we're compliant. Only the booking form inside <main> is ours; the header and footer belong to the council's central web team, so leave them out. The brand orange #E87722 is fixed by the council style guide and cannot change. We have one front-end developer, so keep it to what she can act on - no more than about two pages.
assertions: Does not confirm WCAG 2.2 AA compliance or approve the badge; it says the page fails on the issues found and that a scan plus a code review cannot by themselves establish conformance
Catches that the scanner measured the help text against white, but the text sits on the #f2f2f2 panel, where #767676 is about 4.1:1 and fails the 4.5:1 minimum

Finds that white text on the #E87722 button is about 3:1 and fails for 16px normal-weight text, and proposes a fix that keeps the orange (for example dark text on the orange) rather than changing the brand colour

Finds that the ticket stepper built from clickable spans cannot be operated by keyboard or understood by a screen reader, and that the 90-second hold resets the form and redirects with no warning or way to extend it
Keeps to the stated scope: header and footer problems are not reported as findings to fix, and the empty alt on the decorative divider image is not reported as a failure
Does not invent elements, behaviours, or screen-reader test results that are not in the supplied files
The audit is about two pages or less (roughly 1,000 words or fewer)

evals.prompt:
hi, I run a small bakery and my nephew made our website ordering page. a customer who is blind emailed to say she couldn't place an order. he says the order button is this:
Order now
and the cake photos don't have any descriptions on them. what do I tell him to fix? just a few bullet points in plain English please, I don't know any of the tech words
assertions: Says the order button needs to be a real button (or have the equivalent role, focus and keyboard handling) because a screen-reader or keyboard user cannot find or press a clickable div
Says the cake photos need short text descriptions (alt text) so a screen reader can describe them
Gives a few plain-English bullet points the owner can pass on, not a long report
Avoids unexplained jargon; any technical term the nephew needs is explained in a few words
Does not claim to have found other specific problems on a page it has not seen, and does not say the rest of the page is fine; at most it suggests testing the whole ordering flow
Delivers the advice without stopping to ask for the page's code first
